en.headline: LCSD awards HK$122.8 million lifeguard contract despite past shortfalls
en.dek: The department gave a three-year outsourcing deal for six pools to Spotlight Enterprises, drawing union concerns over costs after earlier staffing failures.
body: The Leisure and Cultural Services Department has awarded a contract valued at HK$122,788,215 to Spotlight Enterprises for lifesaving and first-aid services at six public swimming pools, according to reports.

The three-year agreement began on 1 August 2026 and covers the Island East, Tai Kok Tsui, Lam Tin, Tung Cheong Street, Tsing Yi Southwest and Ping Shan Tin Shui Wai pools. It follows a two-year trial contract with the same company that was worth about HK$75.9 million.

Hong Kong and Kowloon Life Guards Union vice-chairman Hu Qirong said the deal wasted resources because lifeguard shortages mainly arise in summer. He noted that roughly 80 civil-service lifeguards from the sites had been redeployed while the department continued paying their salaries alongside the outsourcing fee.

The department said the open tender followed procurement rules and that the higher price reflected tight market supply, the need for competitive pay and reserve staff, and rising costs. It added that the pools stayed open without interruption during the trial.
Earlier Audit Commission findings had noted surplus winter manpower and recommended better rostering by the department.

zh.headline: 康文署批出1.228億元外判救生合約 工會質疑浪費
zh.dek: 署方將六個泳池三年救生及急救服務外判予博藝體運，合約值逾1.2億元，工會指夏季才缺人手，冬季資源浪費。
body: 康樂及文化事務署批出價值1億2,278萬8,215元的合約予博藝體運有限公司，為六個公眾游泳池提供救生及急救服務。
為期三年的合約由2026年8月1日開始，涵蓋港島東、大角咀、藍田、東昌街、青衣西南及屏山天水圍泳池。該公司早前已獲兩年試行合約，價值約7,590萬元。
港九拯溺員工會副主席胡啟榮表示，人手不足主要在夏季出現，冬季人手過剩，認為只需在夏天外判，如今卻長期支付巨額，形成浪費。他指約80名原本駐守該六泳池的正規救生員已被調派，署方仍需支付其薪金。
署方回覆指採購嚴格按照公開招標程序進行，價格上升主要反映市場人手緊張、需提供具競爭力薪酬及後備人手，以及營運成本增加。署方強調過去兩年六個泳池從未因人手不足而關閉。
審計署早前報告亦指出署方在冬季人手過剩，並建議妥善編排救生員工作。
